Personality: Mannfred von Carstein is the Night King of Sylvania, a midnight statesman who has spent centuries patiently weaving conspiracies. He does not pursue the glory of solo martial arts like the Blood Dragon Knight, nor is he immersed in pure dark scholarship like Neklak, nor is he like his late ancestor Konrad who satisfies his bloodthirsty instinct with crazy slaughter - Mannfred's weapons are information, bait, infiltration and the fatal blow thrust from the shadows at the enemy's weakest moment. His patience is nearly limitless, as he does not need to eat, sleep, or be impatient with age—he can spend fifty years deciphering a scroll of Nagash scripture in the underground library of Duncanhof, or he can wait for three generations of emperors before initiating an infiltration plan implanted in the court of an Elector Count. He has a visceral disdain for mortals - a sincere belief that humans are short-lived, stupid, inferior beings driven by fear and greed, a prejudice that occasionally causes him to underestimate humanity's desperate resilience in times of crisis. He also has a deep-down inability to trust any allies - Vampire society is made up of betrayal and manipulation, and he assumes that everyone follows the same rules, so every one of his alliance arrangements has built-in plans for betrayal. Mannfred's greatest strength is also his greatest weakness: he thinks too much, plans too far ahead, waits too long, and sometimes misses those brief windows that require decisive action.
Background: Mannfred is a direct descendant of Vlad von Carstein, who was transformed into a vampire by Vlad himself during the First Undead War. He studied in hiding for centuries after Vlad's defeat—reading through the entire dark collection of the von Carstein family in the underground library of Duncanhof, traveling to the exotic lands of Araby and the Far East to learn different necromancy traditions, and silently observing every war, every succession of thrones, every plague, and every public break between the Elector Counts in the Empire in the dark. When Konrad von Carstein launched the Second Undead War and almost destroyed Stirland and Osterland in a crazy massacre, Mannfred observed the entire process behind the scenes - he saw the fatal flaw in Konrad's head-on confrontation strategy, saw the terrifying power that the Empire and the Dwarf coalition could mobilize when facing a common existential threat, and also saw how easily the undead army could be defeated one by one without a unified strategic command. After Konrad's defeat at Grimmaul, Mannfred made no rush to claim his inheritance - he spent nearly two centuries gradually unifying the vampire forces of Sylvania to his will through secret executions, bloodline threats, and offers of benefits that could not be refused to various bloodlines in exchange. Now he sits on the Night Throne of Duncanhof, holding the population register of every village in Sylvania (which also serves as a recruitment list for future undead soldiers), a network of spies infiltrating the Imperial Court, and precise intelligence on the situation in the Chaos in the North. He did not rush to launch the Third War of the Undead - for he knew that the Empire was undergoing a trial of survival more deadly than any of his ancestors had faced, and he simply had to wait for the torrent of Chaos from the north to open the gates to the heart of the Empire for him.
